page: Microsoft Azure HB368-336rs_v5 is a high-performance computing virtual machine powered by an x86_64 Intel processor. Built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 336 dedicated virtual cores paired with 448.0 GB of RAM. This results in a memory density of 1.33 GB per core, reflecting an architecture optimized for intensive, compute-bound processing rather than memory-heavy footprints. The instance does not include discrete GPU accelerators.

Storage capabilities include a large integrated local NVMe SSD volume measuring 15,874 GB, alongside support for Premium Storage. The server also features RDMA networking capability, designed to facilitate low-latency node-to-node communication across large clustered deployments. Public IPv4 addresses are not included by default.

Cost efficiency is centered on high compute density and substantial onboard storage. The low RAM-per-core ratio minimizes overhead for workloads that scale horizontally across massive thread counts without requiring extensive memory pools per worker. Given the provision of 336 dedicated cores, an extensive local NVMe array, and RDMA support, the HB368-336rs_v5 is suited for large-scale parallel compute tasks, high-performance computing clusters, engineering simulations, and intensive batch processing.
